root_idea.summary: The evidence does not establish a native Arabic root principle for مجس; it treats the word as a Persian-origin designation associated with the Magians.
root_idea.development: The designation مَجُوس names the Magian community. Related lexical formations include مَجُوسِيّ for an individual Magian, مَجُوسِيَّة for the Magian religion, Form II مَجَّسَ for making someone a Magian or teaching the Magian religion, and Form V تَمَجَّسَ for becoming a Magian.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quranic occurrence is the established collective/proper designation مَجُوس, attested in Lane as the Magians and a certain nation.

senses.definition: The Magians: a named community or nation.
senses.usage_conditions: Used as a collective or plural designation. The lexical discussion describes مَجُوس as either the plural of مَجُوسِيّ or a collective generic noun; in the Quran it occurs as the name of the Magians.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make someone a Magian; to teach someone the religion of the Magians.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form II causative verb; the two explanations describe the related effects of causing affiliation with, or instruction in, the Magian religion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become a Magian; to enter the religion of the Magians.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form V verb expressing adoption of Magian affiliation or religion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An individual Magian; one belonging to the Magian religion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Singular relational noun associated with the collective designation مَجُوس; the lexical description applies it as an epithet to a man.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The religion of the Magians; Magianism.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is also used in a reported theological comparison involving the Qadariyya and the Magians; that comparison does not create a separate denotation.

lane_unit_coverage.note: The Form II causative meanings are represented together.
The Form V meaning of becoming Magian is represented.
The community designation and its singular relational term are represented; historical and etymological remarks add no separate lexical branch.
The religion name is represented; the Qadariyya comparison is treated as contextual usage.

cautions: QAC supplies a Proper noun analysis while also tagging the occurrence with a PASSIVE_PARTICIPLE nominal type; the public headword follows the established lexical designation مَجُوس rather than treating it as an ordinary passive participle.
Lane reports variant Persian etymologies and differing historical identifications concerning the name; these are etymological or historical notes, not additional lexical senses.
